correctness.rationale: Conditioning on one specified cell having occupancy r leaves a uniform allocation of the remaining n-r observations across m-1 cells, giving the conditional expected collision count exactly. Pearson chi-square is affine in pair collisions, so the covariance polynomial follows algebraically. Pair-collision indicators are pairwise independent, yielding the exact Pearson variance. The K_r variance comes from one-cell and two-cell multinomial probabilities. The fixed-load limit follows from fixed-r factorial expansions. Exact allocation enumeration independently reproduces every finite covariance on a parameter grid.

value.rationale: Frequency-of-frequencies counts are canonical occupancy/species-sampling summaries, while Pearson chi-square is the canonical quadratic equal-cell goodness-of-fit statistic. The theorem resolves their full finite coordinate-wise second-moment coupling and exposes a load-dependent sign phase that aggregate richness/collision results cannot show. The singleton threshold n=2m and the fixed-load polynomial provide directly interpretable diagnostics for which occupancy layers drive Pearson fluctuation.
